justice: The carriageway is very wide with multiple motor-vehicle lanes, while no visible sidewalk, crossing, or dedicated pedestrian space appears in the frame, suggesting street space is distributed more strongly toward drivers than toward all users equally.

livability: Continuous rows of mature trees and landscaped medians make the corridor greener and more pleasant than a bare arterial road.

sustainability: The extensive tree canopy along both sides and the planted center median provide urban greenery that can support shade, cooling, and air-quality benefits.

aesthetics: The street has a strong visual order created by straight lane markings, evenly spaced light poles, and continuous planted medians.

comfort: Thermal comfort is relatively good near the edges because mature roadside trees cast visible shade onto the right side of the corridor.

walkability: Walkability is limited because a dedicated sidewalk is not clearly visible in the frame, even though tree-lined edge space suggests one may exist beyond the curb.
